title: Use of vaginal estrogens in urogynecology: current evidence, controversies and clinical applications.
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a prevalent yet underrecognized condition in postmenopausal women, characterized by progressive vulvovaginal and lower urinary tract symptoms from estrogen deficiency. Vaginal estrogen therapy is the first-line pharmacologic treatment for GSM. However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve. This review summarizes current evidence on vaginal estrogen formulations, clinical effectiveness, safety, and therapeutic applications. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent randomized controlled trials confirm that low-dose vaginal estrogen significantly improves GSM symptoms - including vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and irritation - while restoring epithelial integrity and normalizing pH. Evidence also supports its role in reducing recurrent urinary tract infections by restoring lactobacilli-dominant flora, reinforced by a 2025 multisociety clinical guideline recommending topical, but not systemic, estrogen for this indication. Comparative studies show similar efficacy across creams, tablets, inserts, and rings, differing primarily in convenience and absorption rather than effectiveness. Large cohort studies indicate no increased risk of cardiovascular disease, venous thromboembolism, or malignancy. Use in breast cancer survivors remains controversial, but emerging data suggest minimal systemic absorption and no clear increase in recurrence risk, supporting shared decision-making. In addition, long-term outcomes show that adjunctive vaginal estrogen does not improve anatomic surgical success after native tissue apical prolapse repair. Nonhormonal therapies and agents like ospemifene or prasterone offer alternative options, though they demonstrate lower or more variable efficacy than vaginal estrogen. SUMMARY: Vaginal estrogen therapy is the most effective, evidence-based treatment for GSM and helps prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in postmenopausal women. Its favorable safety profile and multiple formulations enable individualized care. Recent evidence clarifies that while overall safety is reassuring, caution is necessary for breast cancer survivors using aromatase inhibitors. Additionally, longer-term perioperative trial data temper expectations regarding surgical-recurrence benefits, while confirming its value for local tissue optimization. Ongoing research should focus on long-term safety in high-risk groups and the effectiveness of emerging non-estrogen alternatives.

title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control. AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE. METHODS: SPIRARE II was a prospective, single-arm, multicentre pivotal investigation conducted at 19 sites in the United States and Europe. Eligible patients had acute PE (≤14 days), a computed tomography angiography-assessed RV to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio>0.9, and haemodynamic stability (systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg). Co-primary endpoints were composite major adverse events (MAE) within 48 hours and core laboratory-assessed RV/LV change from baseline to 48 hours. Prespecified secondary endpoints were collected immediately pre- and post-procedure in all patients including mean pulmonary artery pressure, total pulmonary vascular resistance, and cardiac index. RESULTS: In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours, a mean reduction of 0.39±0.33, exceeding the prespecified performance goal (p<0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System met its prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints in acute intermediate-risk PE. TFX delivered precise, stable control with reliable vessel access, enabling consistent right ventricular unloading. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06576427).

title: Ultrasound-Guided versus Fluoroscopy-Guided Femoral Access for Structural Heart Procedures: Outcomes From Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation and Left Atrial Appendage Closure.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transfemoral access is the default approach for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC). Although ultrasound (US)-guided femoral puncture improves first-pass success and reduces vascular complications in randomized trials, real-world data in contemporary structural heart interventions, including both arterial and venous large-sheath access, remain limited. The authors aimed to compare US-guided vs. conventional transfemoral access in patients undergoing TAVI and LAAC. METHODS: This single-center, retrospective cohort study included 165 consecutive patients undergoing transfemoral structural procedures between January 2022 and December 2024 (93: TAVI; 72: LAAC). Ultrasound guidance was used in 57 procedures (34.5%). Arterial and venous cohorts were analyzed separately. Primary outcomes were absolute hemoglobin decrease (ΔHb) and access-site vascular complications (hematoma, pseudoaneurysm, and arteriovenous fistula). In the arterial cohort, 1 : 1 propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences. RESULTS: Hemoglobin decline was significantly smaller with US guidance in both venous (0.80 ± 0.95 vs. 1.50 ± 1.11 g/dL; P = .009) and arterial procedures (0.58 ± 0.97 vs. 1.29 ± 1.00 g/dL; P = .002). In the venous cohort, complication rates were numerically lower but not statistically different (3.8% vs. 17.4%; P = .143). In contrast, arterial complications were significantly reduced with US guidance. After propensity matching (31 patients per group), complications occurred in 3.2% vs. 29.0% [Absolute Risk Reduction(ARR) = 25.8%, Number Need to Treat (NNT) = 4, P = .013]. CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided transfemoral access was associated with reduced hemoglobin decline and fewer vascular complications, particularly in large-bore arterial procedures, supporting routine integration of real-time US guidance in structural interventions.

title: Access Vessel Patency After Endovascular Therapy via Tibiopedal Access in Patients With Lower Extremity Artery Disease.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the access vessel patency after endovascular therapy performed via tibiopedal access. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a retrospective, single-center, observational study. Patients who underwent endovascular therapy via tibiopedal access with sheath insertion were enrolled. The primary outcome was loss of access vessel patency defined as access vessel occlusion or stenosis with a peak systolic velocity ratio > 2.4 on duplex ultrasound at 6 months. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify the predictors of access vessel patency loss, with hemodialysis, severely calcified access vessel and sheath-to-artery ratio included as covariates. RESULTS: A total of 95 limbs in 91 patients were included in this study, and loss of access vessel patency was observed in 22 limbs (23.1%). Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated that sheath-to-artery ratio was the only independent predictor (odds ratio: 1.493, 95% confidence interval: 1.130-1.976; p = 0.005). The receiver operating characteristic curve analysis revealed that the optimal cutoff value of sheath-to-artery ratio for predicting loss of access vessel patency was 1.08, with an area under the curve of 0.723. In this cohort, the 2-year freedom from major adverse limb events were 98.6% (95% CI: 90.8-99.8%), and no major amputation occurred. CONCLUSION: The present study demonstrated a relatively high incidence of loss of access vessel patency after endovascular therapy via tibiopedal access, although this was not associated with an increase in major adverse limb events. A larger sheath-to-artery ratio was identified as an independent predictor of loss of access vessel patency.

title: Endovascular Salvage of Dysfunctional Native Haemodialysis Arteriovenous Fistulas: Clinical Outcomes and Predictors of Patency.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypofunctioning haemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas are an important cause of inadequate dialysis, access failure and morbidity in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), and timely catheter-based intervention may help restore access function and prolong fistula usability. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy, feasibility, and safety of catheter-based interventional procedures for hypofunctioning haemodialysis fistulas in patients with CKD. METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective observational follow up study, enrolled with 100 CKD patients on maintenance haemodialysis with dysfunctional native arteriovenous fistulas who underwent fistulogram and catheter-based intervention. RESULTS: The mean age was 57.2 ± 12.4 years, 62.0% were male, and hypertension (80.0%) and diabetes mellitus (57.0%) were the major comorbidities. Radio cephalic fistula was the commonest access type (46.0%), and inadequate dialysis was the leading presentation (73.0%). Fistulography showed significant stenosis in 96.0%, with central vein involvement in 43.0% and long-segment lesions in 56.0%. Angioplasty was attempted in 96.0%, achieving technical success in 91.7% of attempted interventions and clinical success in 85.0%. Stenosis and pressure gradient reduced significantly after intervention (both p<0.001). Complications occurred in 13.0%, with no deaths. Primary patency declined from 82.0% at 1 month to 58.0% at 6 months and 38.0% at 12 months. Patency loss was independently predicted by older age, central vein lesions, long lesions, residual stenosis, and absent post-procedure thrill. CONCLUSION: Catheter-based endovascular intervention may be an effective fistula-salvage strategy for hypofunctioning haemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas, although long-term patency was influenced by lesion complexity, residual stenosis and restoration of post-procedure thrill.

title: Percutaneous approach to aortic disease: EVAR, TEVAR and newer techniques for more proximal disease.
abstract: Advances in device design, imaging and vascular-closure technology have driven a progressive shift from surgical femoral exposure to totally percutaneous strategies for endovascular aortic repair. This narrative review summarises contemporary evidence and practical considerations for percutaneous access across the spectrum of aortic disease, from infrarenal endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) to thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), fenestrated/branched repair and endovascular treatment of the aortic arch. Percutaneous femoral access is now supported by randomized evidence, large registries and administrative cohorts showing high technical success, fewer wound complications, shorter operative times and shorter hospital stay compared with routine surgical cutdown, and real-time ultrasound-guided puncture has become a guideline-endorsed standard of care. Major contemporary developments include computed tomography-based access planning centred on calcification burden and sheath-to-artery ratio; an individualised, anatomy-driven choice between suture- and plug-based closure devices; endovascular preparation of hostile iliofemoral anatomy with pave-and-crack, endoconduits and intravascular lithotripsy; low-profile endografts that have widened transfemoral eligibility; and percutaneous axillary and carotid routes that enable complex TEVAR, fenestrated/branched and selected arch repairs in experienced centres, although evidence for these latter applications remains largely observational. Looking ahead, further reductions in delivery-system profile, dedicated large-bore closure technologies, image-fusion guidance and off-the-shelf branched devices are expected to extend fully percutaneous repair to increasingly complex anatomy, while prospective, aortic-specific and device-level comparisons with standardized anatomical metrics and long-term follow-up are needed to refine patient selection and confirm durable limb and target-vessel patency.

title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although "time is brain" remains a core principle in acute stroke care, the association between treatment timing and functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) varies across patients. Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology. METHODS: We analyzed data from two multicenter registries in Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) from January 2019 to April 2023. Patients with anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism (CE) or large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) were included. Multivariable regression and interaction analyses were performed to evaluate the association between onset-to-puncture (OTP) time and 90-day functional outcomes and to identify effect modifiers. RESULTS: _interaction Among 4,719 patients (mean age 72.0 years; 42.9% women; median NIHSS 15), longer OTP time was associated with lower odds of 90-day functional independence (adjusted OR per hour, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.98; p=0.001). The impact of OTP time varied by stroke characteristics. CE etiology, MCA occlusion, higher NIHSS, and male sex were associated with greater time sensitivity. In CE strokes, each hour of delay reduced the odds of functional independence by 4% (aOR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.97; p<0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in LAA strokes (P=0.028). CONCLUSION: The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

title: A pilot study of the InVera Infusion Device: Twelve-month outcomes in the treatment of incompetent saphenous veins.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The InVera Infusion Device is a novel catheter designed for the delivery of sclerosant agents during non-thermal, non-tumescent (NTNT) ablation of incompetent superficial truncal veins of the lower extremity. This device pilot study aimed to evaluate the technical success, safety, and 12-month clinical outcome. METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the InVera Infusion Device. Primary outcomes assessed were technical procedural success, adverse events, Revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), patient-reported outcomes (PROs) based on a HASTI (Heaviness, Achiness, Swelling, Throbbing, Itching) symptom questionnaire and anatomical success rates from duplex ultrasound examination at baseline, 1 week, 8 weeks, 3, 6, and 12 months post procedure. Baseline and 12 months post procedure were compared for both the rVCSS and the HASTI results using a paired t-test and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test respectively RESULTS: Technical procedural success was 100%. There were no device-related adverse events or serious adverse events including no deep vein thrombosis recorded throughout the follow-up period. Clinician assessed rVCSS and patient reported HASTI scores both showed statistically significant reductions from baseline to 12 months (adjusted p = 0.03 for both). Ultrasound-based anatomical assessment at 12 months demonstrated elimination of abnormal reflux and complete or partial occlusion in 90% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: The InVera Infusion device provides a safe and effective technique for the delivery of sclerosant agents as part of the management of incompetent saphenous veins, demonstrating favorable 12-month anatomical, clinical and patient reported outcomes in this pilot cohort.

title: Systematic Review of Devices, Designs, and Trials for the Treatment of Deep Venous Reflux.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) is driven primarily by venous reflux and affects nearly one-third of adults. While superficial reflux is effectively treated with ablation, therapeutic options for deep venous reflux (DVR) remain limited. Despite decades of innovation, no prosthetic or bioprosthetic venous valve has achieved U.S. regulatory approval. We systematically reviewed device strategies, clinical and hemodynamic outcomes, complications, and barriers to translation for devices designed to treat DVR. METHODS: We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251101761) of six databases from inception through February 2026, including in vivo animal and human studies evaluating prosthetic or bioprosthetic devices for DVR. Studies of native valve repair or autotransplantation were excluded. The primary outcome for human studies was clinical improvement, and secondary outcomes included patency, procedural complications, valvular function, and thrombosis. RESULTS: Of 516 records identified, 15 met inclusion criteria: 8 human and 7 animal studies. Two principal strategies were identified: intraluminal valve restoration (VR) and external compression (EC), with approximately 40% of devices delivered percutaneously or endovenously. In human studies, technical success ranged from 87.7%-100%, patency from 67%-100%, and perioperative complication rates from 0%-44%, consisting primarily of bleeding, wound infection, and valve thrombosis. Valve occlusion occurred in up to 28% of animal implants and 18%-22% of select human cohorts. Two perioperative deaths occurred in animal studies; none were reported in human studies. Among human studies, valve competency assessment methods varied substantially. Reported competency ranged from 0%-92%, reflecting heterogeneity in imaging modalities and definitions. Discordance between anatomic patency, duplex-derived reflux reduction, and clinical improvement was frequently observed. In contemporary multicenter trial data, fewer than half of patients met predefined reflux-reduction endpoints despite high device patency and substantial clinical improvement, highlighting discordance between anatomic, hemodynamic, and patient-centered outcomes. By one year, pain had improved in 75%-97% of patients; rVCSS decreased by 37%-81%, with clinically meaningful (≥3-point) improvement in up to 84.6%; and ulcer healing ranged from 67%-100%. Longer follow-up extended to 2 years in animal studies and up to 11 years in human series with various outcomes reported. CONCLUSION: Several devices developed for DVR have demonstrated technical feasibility and symptom improvement. However, the risk of thrombosis, the marginal impact on valvular function, and the lack of standardization and selection of adequate endpoints in the measurement of results remain major barriers to regulatory approval. Standardized composite endpoints integrating objective hemodynamic measures with patient-centered outcomes are essential to advance durable DVR device development and clinical translation.

title: Admission C-Reactive Protein-to-Albumin Ratio Is Associated With Early Major Amputation After Minor Amputation in Patients With Infected Foot Wounds.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Minor amputation is commonly performed as a limb-salvage procedure for infected foot wounds; however, some patients experience early limb-salvage failure and progress to major amputation. Reliable biomarkers predicting early failure remain limited. PURPOSE: To evaluate whether the admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) is associated with major amputation within 90 days after minor amputation in patients with infected foot wounds. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. METHODS: Patients who underwent minor amputation for infected foot wounds between March 2005 and September 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Of 358 screened patients, 257 met the inclusion criteria. Admission CAR was calculated from C-reactive protein and serum albumin levels. The primary outcome was major amputation within 90 days. Univariable logistic regression and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. RESULTS: Among 257 patients, 60 (23.3%) progressed to major amputation within 90 days. Higher admission CAR values were significantly associated with major amputation. CAR remained an independent predictor in multivariable analysis (hazard ratio 1.17; 95% confidence interval 1.05-1.31; p value = .004). Adding CAR improved the predictive performance of the baseline model (area under the curve .883 vs .810). CONCLUSIONS: Admission CAR is a simple and independent factor associated with early major amputation after minor amputation and may help facilitate early risk stratification. LEVEL OF CLINICAL EVIDENCE: Level III.

title: Collapse and Thrombosis of an Iliac Branch Endovascular Device Following Blunt Force Trauma.
abstract: Iliac branch endovascular device thrombosis following blunt force trauma has rarely been reported. We describe an 81-year-old man who developed proximal aortobiiliac endograft collapse with subsequent thrombosis after blunt force trauma occurring two months following endovascular aneurysm repair. The patient delayed vascular follow-up for one year and later presented at routine surveillance with progressive bilateral hip and buttock claudication. Despite chronic therapeutic anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation, the patient developed progressive thrombosis with ischemic symptoms. The case highlights a rare mechanical cause of post-EVAR aortoiliac thrombosis and demonstrates the importance of early vascular imaging and consultation following traumatic injury in post-EVAR patients.

abstract: 2 P ObjectiveTo compare diameter- and volume-based surveillance after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and determine whether volumetric sac assessment identifies postoperative remodeling not captured by conventional maximum diameter measurement.MethodsThis retrospective single-center study included 383 patients who underwent elective EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm between January 2016 and April 2024. Maximum sac diameter, total aneurysm sac volume, thrombus volume, thrombus density, neck morphology, and other anatomical variables were assessed using standardized morphometric and three-dimensional morphovolumetric measurements. Sac dynamics were classified by diameter criteria (≥5 mm decrease, stable, or ≥5 mm increase) and volumetric criteria (>10% decrease, stable, or >10% increase).ResultsEndoleaks occurred in 26.1% of patients (n = 100), and secondary interventions were required in 14.1% (n = 54), with a mean time to reintervention of 21.7 ± 10 months. At final follow-up, 74.7% demonstrated sac diameter reduction, 18.5% were stable, and 6.8% had enlargement, whereas volumetric analysis showed shrinkage in 81.7%, stability in 6.0%, and enlargement in 12.3%. At 1, 6, and 12 months, cohort mean diameter changed by -0.6%, -3.1%, and -6.5% from baseline, respectively, while cohort mean volume changed by -0.5%, -5.7%, and -12.5%. Among diameter-stable sacs, 32.4% enlarged volumetrically and 38.0% regressed volumetrically. In enlarging sacs, a 10% volume increase corresponded to an approximately 4 mm diameter increase (R= 0.72;< 0.001); this 4 mm value was a regression estimate, not the diameter threshold used for sac classification. Preoperative morphometric and morphovolumetric variables were associated with endoleak and secondary intervention in exploratory analyses.ConclusionVolumetric sac analysis identified additional postoperative remodeling beyond maximum diameter measurement, particularly in apparently stable sacs. A practical surveillance strategy combining rapid diameter-based screening with selective volumetric analysis in stable, borderline, or clinically suspicious cases may improve recognition of adverse sac behavior without requiring routine volumetry in every follow-up study.

title: Initial Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Warfarin After Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Target Trial Emulation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists have traditionally been used after cerebral venous thrombosis, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly prescribed. Whether DOACs are noninferior to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015-2022; prospective phase, 2023-2025). Eligible patients were adults with imaging-confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis who initiated either a DOAC or warfarin within 30 days after diagnosis. Time zero was the date of the first oral anticoagulant prescription. The primary efficacy outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE within 1 year. Propensity score overlap weighting was used, and weighted Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event. The clinically acceptable noninferiority margin was defined as an absolute increase of 1.5 percentage points in 1-year recurrent VTE risk, corresponding approximately to a relative margin of 1.50 for the primary Fine-Gray analysis. RESULTS: P P Among 2476 eligible patients, 942 initiated a DOAC (rivaroxaban, n=701; dabigatran, n=121; apixaban, n=113; edoxaban, n=7) and 1534 initiated warfarin. Within 1 year, symptomatic recurrent VTE occurred in 36 and 73 patients, respectively. The overlap-weighted 1-year recurrence risks were 3.74% and 5.47%, corresponding to a risk difference of -1.73 percentage points (95% CI, -3.76 to 0.30). DOAC treatment was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard ratio of 0.67 compared with that of warfarin ([95% CI, 0.37-1.21];=0.184), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion (for noninferiority=0.004). Major bleeding was rare within 1 year (0 versus 1 patient). Clinical nonmajor bleeding occurred in 18 versus 34 patients, and any bleeding occurred in 48 versus 75 patients. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with cerebral venous thrombosis selected for oral anticoagulation, initial treatment with a DOAC met the noninferiority criterion relative to warfarin for the prevention of symptomatic recurrent VTE at 1 year. Findings regarding bleeding outcomes were exploratory and do not permit conclusions regarding comparative safety or equivalence.

title: Predictors of Surveillance Imaging Non-compliance Among Patients with TEVAR for Blunt Thoracic Aortic Injury.
abstract: P P ObjectivesBlunt Thoracic Aortic Injury (BTAI) is the second leading cause of death for patients with blunt trauma. Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) has become the standard of care for high-grade BTAI, reducing morbidity and mortality while requiring long-term surveillance imaging to ensure graft integrity and prevent future complications. However, adherence to this protocol is poor. Previous studies evaluating the factors associated with post-operative imaging non-compliance have yielded conflicting results. This study aimed to evaluate predictors of post-TEVAR non-compliance inpatients presenting with BTAI.MethodsA retrospective study on 23 patients was conducted using a single institution Aortic Center Database (2015-2025). Inclusion criteria included patients who were age >18 years and underwent TEVAR for BTAI. Demographic, comorbidity, hospital course, and follow-up data were collected. The Distressed Communities Index (DCI) score was derived from patient's home address ZIP code. Time-to-event analysis defined loss to follow up (LTFU) for vascular imaging as the failure event. Patients were censored at death or if compliant through 1 year following the index TEVAR. Statistical analysis included chi-square, t-tests, and Kaplan-Meier survival.ResultsBased on this single-center review on TEVAR follow-up for BTAI, sex, race, and hospital length of stay did not impact compliance. Medical comorbidities were also non-significant. Patients who presented with a lower injury severity score (= 0.02) and lived more than 20 miles from their follow-up appointment (= 0.02) were more likely to be LTFU. While the type of facility was not impactful, all patients who were discharged to a non-home location were LTFU. Interestingly, DCI and insurance status had no impact on follow-up non-compliance.ConclusionsThis study supports the development of targeted, patient-centered surveillance strategies, especially amongst rural populations and those discharged to a non-home location. To fully understand this complex problem, further investigation using a larger database may be indicated.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

title: MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) Variant Associated With Hereditary Thoracic Aortic Diseases and Early Onset Aortic Dissection.
abstract: AIMS: Thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections are major causes of sudden cardiovascular death. We aimed to evaluate the clinical significance of the MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) variant in Finnish families with heritable thoracic aortic disease (HTAD) and to assess evidence for a potential founder effect. METHODS: We evaluated the clinical significance and potential founder effect of the missense variant MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) in Finnish families. Eight individuals from four unrelated Finnish families carrying the MYLK c.4079G>A heterozygous variant were recruited. Clinical histories, imaging data, and pedigrees were reviewed. Genetic testing included exome‑based gene panel sequencing or targeted familial variant testing. Variant classification followed the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics 2015 guidelines. RESULTS: Thoracic aortic dilatation or aneurysm occurred in 6/8 carriers (75%), with a mean age at diagnosis of 45 years (range 34-67). Ascending aortic diameters ranged from 26-59 mm, most often measured at the aortic root. Aortic dissection occurred in 4/8 (50%) at a mean age of 46 years (range 34-68), including three early‑adult events. Extrathoracic arterial involvement (carotid) was observed in one variant‑positive individual. CONCLUSION: The MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) variant was present in six affected individuals from four unrelated families and is enriched in the Finnish population, supporting a founder effect. The MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) variant is associated with early‑adult‑onset, high‑penetrance thoracic aortic disease and substantial dissection risk, underscoring the need for vigilant surveillance and early intervention in affected individuals and at‑risk relatives.

title: Reported items and methods for analysis in diagnostic management studies evaluating venous thromboembolism: a systematic review: Communication from the ISTH SSC Subcommittee on Diagnosis and Prediction in Thrombotic Disease.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Reporting of venous thromboembolism (VTE) diagnostic management studies is not standardized, which contributes to incomplete and variable description of study methods and results. This variability hampers interpretation and appraisal of study results. The aim of this study was to evaluate the reporting of key methodology items in recent VTE diagnostic management studies. METHODS: st th A systematic search was conducted in Embase and MEDLINE from January 1, 2005, to August 6, 2024, to identify prospective diagnostic management studies that included adult patients with suspected VTE with follow-up of patients in whom VTE was excluded at baseline. The primary outcome was the reporting of predefined study items. Secondary outcomes were definitions and analysis of diagnostic failure rates and efficiency. RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies were included. Reporting varied: study design, inclusion criteria, follow-up and overall VTE prevalence were consistently reported, whereas location of confirmed PE and reasons for loss to follow-up were poorly reported. Fifty-four studies (92%) reported a definition of the diagnostic failure rate, of which 45 (83%) defined it as the incidence of VTE in all patients in whom VTE had been excluded at baseline. Predefined upper safety margin for the diagnostic failure rate was reported in 34 studies (63%), and varied widely, ranging between 1.5% and 8.0%. Only 8 studies (14%) defined diagnostic efficiency. CONCLUSION: Reporting of key study items, as well as definitions and analysis of diagnostic failure rates varied among VTE diagnostic management studies. Standardization of the reporting and analysis of VTE diagnostic management studies is needed.

title: Incidence of thrombosis and bleeding in patients with JAK2- positive myeloproliferative neoplasms receiving low-dose aspirin: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with JAK2V617F-positive myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are at increased thrombotic risk and commonly receive low-dose aspirin, yet its net clinical benefit is uncertain. OBJECTIVES: We estimated the incidence of thrombotic and bleeding events in patients with JAK2-positive MPNs treated with low-dose aspirin. METHODS: A systematic review was performed for studies evaluating thrombotic and hemorrhagic events in patients with JAK2V617F-positive MPNs while taking low-dose aspirin. Study-level incidence rates (IR) per 100 person-years (PY) and incidence rate ratios (IRR) comparing aspirin use versus no aspirin were calculated and pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 We included 3 randomized clinical trials and 7 observational studies (n=1,760 with aspirin, n=367 without aspirin). The pooled IR of thrombotic events in JAK2V617F-positive MPN patients receiving low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 2.72 per 100 PY (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.59 - 4.65; I=93%) with pooled IRR receiving aspirin versus no aspirin of 0.59 (95% CI 0.40 - 0.86, I=16%). The pooled IR of major and non-major bleeding on low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 1.97 (95% CI 1.06 - 3.65; I=90%) per 100 PY with pooled IRR of 2.43 (95% CI 1.15 - 5.11; I=43%). The GRADE level of confidence for the investigated risks was low. CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin was associated with a 40% reduction in thrombosis but a 2.5-fold increase in bleeding risk with low certainty of evidence. More studies are needed to gain high-quality evidence the better define the role of aspirin in JAK2V617F-positive MPNs.

title: Sex-related differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes of ischemic stroke following thrombectomy: data from an inverse propensity score weighted analysis.
abstract: PURPOSE: We investigated sex differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes among ischemic stroke patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT) within 24 h from last known well. METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set. We performed univariable analyses to identify baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes that differed between sexes. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess whether sex was associated with outcomes after adjusting for covariates. RESULTS: Among 615 patients included in the analysis, 318 (51.7%) were female. Compared to females, males were younger (p <0.001), more independent before stroke (p <0.001), had a lower prevalence of atrial fibrillation (p < 0.001), and had lower internal carotid artery occlusion (p < 0.013). Compared to male, females had lower total hypoperfused tissue (109.3 mL [IQR=66.4-151.3] vs. 86.3 mL [IQR=43.4-132.3]; p<0.001), lower penumbra volumes (78.1 mL [IQR=43.9-114.8] vs. 47.7 mL [IQR=24.6-76.6], p<0.001), lower mismatch ratio (2.63 [IQR=1.86-4.49] vs. 3.67 [IQR=2.27-6.53]; p<0.001), and lower hypoperfusion intensity ratio (0.30 [IQR=0.18-0.50] vs. 0.38 [IQR=0.22-0.50]; p<0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, sex was not an independent predictor of good clinical outcomes after EVT, although females died less than males and had a lower incidence of hemorrhagic transformation. CONCLUSION: In our cohort of acute ischemic stroke treated with EVT, females showed an overall better perfusion profile at baseline compared to males, suggesting they may be slow progressors; however, this did not translate into better clinical outcomes. More data are needed to clarify the relationship between neuroimaging and sex, as well as the influence of other clinical factors on outcomes among patients undergoing EVT.

title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year. RESULTS: P P Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively;=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]);for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin. CONCLUSIONS: Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.

title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: 2 2 2 2 This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m). title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO. METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. RESULTS: P Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted<0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]). CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required. title: Omega-6 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Peripheral Artery Disease: An Individual Participant-Level Analysis of 9 International Prospective Studies.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have previously been associated with several peripheral artery disease (PAD) risk factors. We studied the association between individual omega-6 PUFAs and incident PAD in a multicohort analysis. METHODS: This study was conducted among participants from 9 cohorts (N=137 704; PAD cases=2014) in the FORCE (Fatty Acids and Outcomes Research Consortium) who were free of clinical PAD at baseline. Omega-6 PUFAs were measured at baseline and with a median follow-up of 14 years. Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were conducted in individual cohorts to evaluate associations of omega-6 PUFAs (continuous cohort-standardized interquintile ranges [difference between the medians of the 10th and 90th omega-6 PUFAs percentiles] and cohort-specific quintiles) with incident clinical PAD adjusting for prespecified covariates. Inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis was used to calculate the combined hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs. RESULTS: P Linoleic acid (LA) was measured in all 9 cohorts, arachidonic acid in 8 (N=33 541; PAD cases=1766), dihomo-γ-LA and γ-LA in 7 (N=29 861; PAD cases=1686), and eicosadienoic acid in 6 (N=27 538; PAD cases=1435). Only LA was associated with a lower risk of incident PAD (quintile 5 versus quintile 1: HR, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.64-0.89];=0.0009). Results did not differ in a statistically significant manner by age, sex, diabetes status, or smoking status. CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that the omega-6 PUFA LA may be protective against PAD, and other omega-6 PUFAs are not associated with PAD incidence. This is further evidence that omega-6 PUFA-disease relationships should be evaluated by individual fatty acids rather than grouped as total omega-6 PUFAs.

title: COG5 Whole-Genome Sequencing and Single-Cell Transcriptomics Identify Human Leukocyte Antigen Loci and aVariant in Aortic Dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic dissection (AD) is a lethal cardiovascular emergency with a complex and underexplored genetic basis. METHODS: We performed whole-genome sequencing on 151 patients with sporadic Stanford type B AD and 965 healthy controls in a Chinese population as a discovery phase analysis to assess both common and rare variants. Cross-ancestry meta-analyses incorporating 4 external genome-wide association data sets were used to identify population-specific risk loci. To pinpoint functional candidates, we integrated epigenomic profiles and single-cell transcriptomes from human aortic tissues. RESULTS: HLA-A HLA-DQA2 COG5 TPM4 Whole-genome sequencing analysis identified 21 candidate common loci and 2 low-frequency variants associated with AD in this discovery cohort. Two candidate common variants in the human leukocyte antigen region (rs9260945 nearand rs9276409 within) showed strong associations and colocalized with regulatory elements in aortic and immune cells, indicating immune-mediated vascular pathology. A low-frequency missense variant in thegene (rs1203229795, effect allele frequency=0.019) emerged as an independent AD risk factor, likely affecting extracellular matrix glycosylation. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of AD-associated variants in human aortic tissues demonstrated enhanced interactions among fibroblasts, vascular smooth muscle cells, and macrophages, supporting their roles in AD pathogenesis. Integrated gene-based and expression analyses further highlighted, a marker of vascular smooth muscle cell dedifferentiation, as a putative susceptibility gene in AD. CONCLUSIONS: COG5 This multiomics investigation expands the genetic landscape of sporadic AD in Chinese individuals, revealing immune-related human leukocyte antigen loci and a functionally supported candidatevariant. Our findings offer new insights into AD pathogenesis and identify candidate targets for future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

title: How far are vision-free medical robots from achieving trustworthy embodied intelligence?
abstract: Embodied Intelligence (EI) is rapidly reshaping the field of robotic surgery, enabling unprecedented levels of clinical precision while liberating surgeons from excessive cognitive and physical burdens. However, for "vision-free" surgical robots incapable of integrating direct visual sensing-such as endovascular robots and untethered swarms-their persistent reliance on external medical imaging fundamentally impedes their evolution toward safe and trustworthy EI-surgery.

title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

title: Laser cryo-sclerotherapy versus conventional sclerotherapy for reticular veins and telangiectasias: A randomized controlled trial.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether the hybrid laser cryo-sclerotherapy (LCS; Nd:Y-AG 1064 nm + 75% hypertonic glucose [HG]) protocol produces superior aesthetic outcomes compared with combined conventional sclerotherapy (CS: 67.5% glucose + 0.3% polidocanol [POL]) for the treatment of lower limb reticular veins and telangiectasias (CEAP C1). METHODS: For this single-center, prospective randomized controlled trial, 60 patients were assessed for eligibility; 4 did not provide informed consent and were not randomized. A total of 56 female patients with CEAP C1 disease and Fitzpatrick phototypes I-III were randomized, with only one lower limb treated per participant: 32 to the LCS group (Nd:YAG 1064 nm + HG75%) and 24 to the CS group (HG67.5% + POL0.3%). Two participants who underwent LCS were subsequently lost to follow-up between Day 1 and Day 30; 54 participants (30 and 24 from the LCS and CS groups, respectively) completed the 90-day follow-up and were analyzed per protocol. Standardized photographs were obtained on Day 1, Day 30, and Day 90, with and without augmented reality (AR; VeinViewer Flex), and were assessed by two blinded external vascular physicians using the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale (GAIS). Complications, residual pigmentation, and quality of life (Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire) were evaluated as secondary end points. RESULTS: Both groups had equivalent baseline characteristics. The LCS group was superior to the CS group in all GAIS outcomes: D1→D90 without AR (P = .026; r = 0.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.04-0.58; moderate effect); D1→D90 with AR (P < .001; r = 0.53; 95% CI, 0.28-0.72; large effect); D30→D90 without AR (P < .001; r = 0.56; 95% CI, 0.31-0.74; large effect); D30→D90 with AR (P < .001; r = 0.52; 95% CI, 0.26-0.71; large effect). After Bonferroni correction for these four primary comparisons (α = .0125), the D1→D90 comparison without AR no longer reached significance, whereas the remaining three comparisons did. Temporal analysis revealed a progressive late aesthetic response in the LCS group; 80.0% of participants continued improving between Day 30 and Day 90 vs 29.1% in the CS group (70.8% with No Change). The ecchymosis duration was significantly shorter in the LCS group (median, 5.0 vs 10.0 days; P = .012). Severe pigmentation on Day 90 was observed exclusively in the CS group (8.3% vs 0%; P = .019; r = 0.22; small effect; power = 36.4%; this finding is exploratory, see the Discussion section). No cases of deep vein thrombosis or ulcer occurred. Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire score improvement was significant in both groups (P < .001), with no intergroup difference. Inter-rater agreement was substantial to near-perfect for GAIS assessments (κ = 0.735-0.913) and perfect for complication grading (κ = 1.000). CONCLUSIONS: The LCS protocol was superior to CS in all GAIS outcomes, with moderate-to-large effect sizes and consistent inter-rater agreement. The aesthetic response was progressive, consolidating between Day 30 and Day 90, with the largest effect size in the late period. AR amplified the magnitude of the detected effects and improved inter-rater agreement, reinforcing its role as a standardizing tool in aesthetic phlebology randomized controlled trials. These statistical findings should be weighed against the higher costs and complexity of LCS relative to CS in a purely cosmetic CEAP C1 population (see the Discussion section).

title: Hybrid pin penetration open stent technique: Retrospective study of a new approach to frozen elephant trunk procedure.
abstract: Total arch replacement using the frozen elephant trunk technique for acute type A aortic dissection involving the aortic arch remains technically demanding because of complex supra-aortic branch reconstruction and prolonged circulatory arrest. We developed a modified fenestrated open stent technique, termed the hybrid pin-penetration open stent (HIPPOS) technique, to simplify branch reconstruction while minimizing supra-aortic vessel manipulation. We retrospectively reviewed 15 consecutive patients who underwent total arch replacement using HIPPOS between May 2024 and May 2026 at a single institution by a single surgeon. Following deployment of a Frozenix open stent graft (Japan Lifeline), antegrade fenestrations were created under direct vision using needle penetration and sequential dilation, followed by reconstruction with balloon-expandable covered stent grafts. All procedures were successfully completed. Operative durations decreased with increasing numbers of fenestrations, reflecting procedural refinement and the surgical learning curve. Two perioperative deaths occurred in patients with profound preoperative shock, and one patient experienced a nondisabling stroke. No postoperative hoarseness, paraplegia, fenestration-related endoleak, or distal stent-induced new entry was observed. Follow-up computed tomography angiography confirmed satisfactory graft conformability and durable branch patency. HIPPOS is a reproducible modification of the frozen elephant trunk procedure with encouraging early clinical outcomes.

title: National Impact of Virtual Residency Interview Format on the Integrated Vascular Surgery Match.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Due to the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) required that residency interviews be conducted virtually, instead of the traditional in-person format. Previous survey studies have indicated that vascular surgery (VS) residency applicants favor remote interviews, noting sufficient exposure to the program, location and residents, with minimal travel-related cost and time burden. However, the overall impact of the virtual interview on objective measures of VS residency match have not been examined. DESIGN: Residency application and match-related data were collected from National Resident Matching Program (NRMP) Main Residency Match reports. In-person interview cycles (2010-2019) were compared with virtual interview cycles (2020-2024). Metrics of VS specialty popularity included total applicants per position and position fill rate. Metrics of VS competitiveness included overall match rate, first-choice match rate, and proportion of unmatched applicants. SETTING: NRMP interview cycles from 2010 to 2024. PARTICIPANTS: All VS residency applicants from 2010 to 2024. RESULTS: The total number of VS programs (68.8 ± 7.9 vs 42.3 ± 11.2), positions (86.2 ± 10.2 vs 48.8 ± 14.3), and applicants (164.8 ± 10.6 vs 96.3 ± 18.3) were significantly higher during the virtual interview cycles (p < 0.001 each). Similar increases were noted in total ACGME-accredited programs, positions, and applicants (p < 0.001 each). Measures of VS specialty popularity, including applicants per position (1.9 ± 0.3 vs 2.1 ± 0.5, p = 0.54) and position fill rate (99.1% ± 1.1% vs 97.2% ± 2.9%, p = 0.20), remained unchanged when comparing in-person and virtual interview cycles. In comparison, the proportion of applicants per position (1.8 ± 0.0 vs 1.9 ± 0.1) and position fill rate (93.9% ± 0.8% vs 95.9% ± 0.5%) across all ACGME-accredited programs were both significantly lower during the virtual interview years (p < 0.001 each). At the same time, the percentage of overall applicants applying into VS increased from 0.18% (±0.03%) to 0.26% (±0.02%) in the virtual era (p < 0.001). Three metrics for specialty competitiveness were also examined. For VS residency programs, overall match rate (52.0% ± 7.1% vs 48.7% ± 10.2%, p = 0.53) and percentage of unmatched applicants (48.0% ± 7.1% vs 51.3% ± 10.2%, p = 0.53) remained unchanged, whereas the proportion of applicants matching at their first choice (41.5% ± 2.9% vs 59.2% ± 13.5%, p = 0.01) was lower during the virtual interview cycles. In comparison, overall match rate was greater (53.2% ± 0.8% vs 49.3 ± 2.1%) and the proportion of unmatched applicants were lower (46.8% ± 0.8% vs 50.7% ± 2.1%, p = 0.001) across all ACGME-accredited programs during the virtual interview years. CONCLUSIONS: The study period of virtual recruitment saw no change in VS popularity, suggesting that this approach does not detract interested applicants. However, VS did become a more competitive residency, with fewer applicants matching at their first choice. Potential hybrid approaches, such as the protocol described within the VISIT trial, may offer viable alternatives that capitalize on the strengths of both virtual recruitment and face-to-face engagement.

title: Real-world thrombotic and survival outcomes with ESAs in cancer-related anemia.
abstract: P P P P Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) are commonly used to treat cancer-related anemia by increasing hemoglobin levels and reducing transfusion requirements. However, randomized trials and meta-analyses have linked ESA use to increased thrombotic risk. Contemporary real-world data across diverse cancer populations and ESA formulations remain limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network (from 1 January 2015 to 31 July 2024) evaluating adult patients with cancer-related anemia. Patients receiving ESAs were propensity score-matched 1:1 with patients not receiving ESAs based on demographics, cancer type, and comorbidities. Individuals with previous thrombotic events or anticoagulant use were excluded. Outcomes included incident deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), new anticoagulant use, and 1-year survival. Risk differences, relative risks, and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were performed. After matching, 1606 patients were included in each cohort, with prostate, breast, bladder, colon, and kidney cancers being the predominant cancer. There was no significant difference in DVT (1.5% vs 2.1%;= .19) or PE (0.75% vs 1.1%;= .27) between ESA and non-ESA groups. New anticoagulant use was significantly lower in patients treated with ESAs (6.3% vs 10.2%; risk ratio, 0.52; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.49-0.78;< .001). One-year survival was higher in the ESA cohort (73% vs 69%; hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.72-0.94;= .004). In this large real-world cohort, ESA use was not associated with increased short-term thrombotic risk and was associated with lower anticoagulant use and improved 1-year survival. These findings suggest that guideline-concordant ESA use may be safe in selected patients with cancer-related anemia.

title: A single-center before-and-after study of physiology-first algorithmic surveillance versus standard observation for arteriovenous fistula maturation.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether a structured, physiology-first surveillance protocol improves arteriovenous fistula clinical maturation rates and reduces time to cannulation readiness compared with standard postoperative observation. METHODS: Two consecutive cohorts of surgically created arteriovenous fistulas by a single surgeon at a community-based center were compared: a standard observation cohort (January-May 2025; 64 created, 58 analyzable) and a physiology-first cohort (June 2025-March 2026; 52 created, all analyzable) managed with a structured protocol featuring standardized 2.7-mm anastomosis, day-of-creation baseline flow documentation, structured ultrasound surveillance at weeks 2 and 4, and defined failure-to-progress intervention triggers and procedure. Salvage intervention for both cohorts included kinetic endovascular micro-incision creation followed by angioplasty with a drug-coated balloon. RESULTS: P P Overall maturation increased from 75.9% (44/58) to 92.3% (48/52;= .022). Unassisted maturation rose from 53.4% (31/58) to 69.2% (36/52). The overall median time to clinical maturation decreased from 49 days (interquartile range, 42-68) to 30 days (interquartile range, 26-43;< .001). Salvage intervention success was comparable between cohorts. Day-of-creation flow documentation increased from 0% to 100%, and no steal syndrome was observed (0/52) with the new physiology-first protocol. CONCLUSIONS: As a quality-improvement evaluation, the physiology-first protocol generated a clear and consistent signal of improved maturation outcomes: access failure decreased, unassisted maturation increased, overall maturation increased, and median time to cannulation readiness decreased. These findings support adopting the protocol as a meaningful adjunct to care and warrant multicenter evaluation.

title: Machine learning-derived serum carbon dioxide trajectories in predicting prognosis of patients with acute aortic dissection.
abstract: Venous partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PvCO 2 ) indicates postoperative adverse outcomes in patients with acute aortic dissection, and its trajectories over time affecting postoperative adverse outcomes remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between PvCO 2 trajectories and postoperative adverse outcomes, as well as clinical application through group-based trajectory modeling and machine-learning algorithms. This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from 642 patients with acute aortic dissection treated at the Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University from 2019 to 2024, to determine postoperative adverse outcomes, including 6-month mortality and complications. Three PvCO 2 tests within the first 72 hours of admission were used to analyze PvCO 2 trajectories through group-based trajectory modeling. To diagnose high-risk PvCO 2 trajectories in emergency settings, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was conducted to select key features, which were consequently integrated into predictive models using multiple machine-learning methods. Finally, a web-based interpretable website was developed for predicting PvCO 2 trajectories in patients with acute aortic dissection. Overall, 642 patients were classed into four PvCO 2 trajectories (T1, persistent decrease from a medium to a low level; T2, stable low level; T3, persistent decrease from a high to a low level; T4, stable midlevel), showing distinct patterns. After adjustment for other covariates, postoperative adverse outcomes among these groups showed significant differences, with a higher proportion of postoperative adverse outcomes in the T3 group. Subsequently, upon Shapley additive explanations analysis, 17 features with importance sequence were identified (hemoglobin, direct bilirubin, monocyte, adenosine deaminase, drinking, anion gap, chloride, platelet, lymphocyte, albumin/globulin ratio, calcium, alanine aminotransferase, α-L-fucosidase, D-dimer, antihypertensive drugs, and smoking), which were integrated into the model for predicting T3. The optimal machine-learning model was established for predicting postoperative adverse outcomes. Finally, a web-based interpretable model was developed to predict patients with acute aortic dissection and high risk of postoperative adverse outcomes. This study uncovers heterogeneity in PvCO 2 trajectory, highlighting that decreased PvCO 2 is associated with worse prognosis. A web-based tool for the prediction of acute aortic dissection patients at high risk of postoperative adverse outcomes was constructed to facilitate clinical application.

title: Risk Factors for Deep Vein Thrombosis After Surgery in Patients with Gastric or Colorectal Cancer Receiving Anticoagulant Prophylaxis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to identify perioperative predictors of early postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in patients undergoing surgery for gastric or colorectal cancer who received routine pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis and to develop a nomogram for postoperative risk stratification. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with gastric or colorectal cancer undergoing surgery from December 2020 to October 2023. All received postoperative low-molecular-weight heparin prophylaxis, and DVT was screened by ultrasonography on postoperative day 3. Predictors were identified by logistic regression and incorporated into a nomogram. RESULTS: A total of 388 eligible patients were included, among whom 124 (32.0%) had screening-detected postoperative lower-extremity DVT. Among patients with DVT, 118 (95.2%) had distal-only DVT and 114 (91.9%) were asymptomatic. Multivariable logistic regression identified age, activated partial thromboplastin time, prothrombin time, and postoperative day 1 D-dimer as independent predictors of postoperative DVT. The nomogram showed acceptable discrimination, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.787 (95% confidence interval 0.731-0.844) in the training cohort and 0.854 (95% confidence interval 0.774-0.934) in the validation cohort. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed risks. In decision curve analysis, the nomogram provided greater net benefit for risk classification than strategies classifying all or no patients as high risk. CONCLUSION: Age, activated partial thromboplastin time, prothrombin time, and postoperative day 1 D-dimer were independently associated with screening-detected early postoperative DVT. The resulting nomogram may help postoperative risk stratification and closer surveillance; however, external validation is required before routine clinical application.

title: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) vs standard care in peptic ulcer perforation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peptic ulcer perforation, although infrequently diagnosed, constitutes a severe condition that necessitates prompt surgical intervention, regardless of whether conservative or surgical management is pursued. The conventional (standard) postoperative care protocol, characterized by delayed feeding, is typically employed for perioperative management. This study sought to review the existing literature comparing the enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) pathway with the standard approach, following both open and laparoscopic Graham repair for peptic ulcer perforation. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Springer, the Cochrane Library, and other resources for studies published over the past 15 years (2011-2026). The selected studies compared the enhanced recovery pathway with the conventional approach for peptic ulcer perforation. A meta-analysis was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyzes guidelines. The risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and funnel plots. Statistical analyzes were performed using Chocrane Review Manager version 5.4. RESULTS: Twelve studies involving 963 patients were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated that patients who underwent enhanced recovery after peptic ulcer perforation surgery exhibited significantly improved clinical outcomes. The length of hospitalization was significantly reduced (0.65; 95% CI, 0.49-0.87; P =.003). The rates of pulmonary complications, venous thromboembolism (0.25; 95% CI, 0.14-0.47; P <.0001), and superficial and deep surgical site infections (0.47; 95% CI, 0.34-0.66; P <.0001 and 0.36; 95% CI, 0.17-0.77; P =.008, respectively) were lower than those in the standard pathway group. CONCLUSION: This systematic review and meta-analysis indicate that the enhanced recovery pathway for peptic ulcer perforation is associated with reduced morbidity and shorter hospital stays compared with the standard pathway. Furthermore, perioperative complications in the ERAS group were lower than those in the conventional group.

title: Factors associated with patency loss after iliocaval and iliofemoral venous stenting.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The factors influencing patency loss after iliocaval and iliofemoral venous stenting remain incompletely understood. We therefore conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize the available evidence. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched to December 2025. Studies reporting associations between potential risk factors and stent outcomes were included. Data were synthesized narratively, and random-effects meta-analyses with Hartung-Knapp adjustment were performed when comparable multivariable-adjusted estimates were available. RESULTS: A total of 49 studies were included, predominantly involving retrospective cohorts. The meta-analysis suggested that post-thrombotic disease, stent extension across or below the inguinal ligament, and hyperlipidemia were associated with an increased risk of patency loss, whereas increasing age showed a modest inverse association with patency loss. The narrative evidence suggested that greater anatomical disease extent was associated with poorer stent patency, whereas the evidence regarding impaired venous inflow was heterogeneous and varied according to the disease phenotype, anatomical segment, and inflow definition. Pooled analyses did not identify statistically significant associations of sex, stent length, or number of stents with patency loss. Evidence regarding anticoagulation discontinuation and adjunctive antiplatelet therapy was insufficient and inconsistent. CONCLUSIONS: Patency loss after iliocaval and iliofemoral venous stenting appears to be associated with the disease phenotype, higher anatomical disease burden, and stent landing strategy. Venous inflow impairment may also be associated with poorer stent patency, although the evidence was heterogeneous. The predominantly retrospective evidence precludes causal inference. Prospective studies with standardized definitions and robust adjustment are needed to improve risk stratification and optimize post-stenting management.

title: Key factors for predicting outcomes one year after Meso-Rex bypass surgery and optimizing the surgical plan in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To analyze the factors for predicting 1-year outcomes and optimize surgical planning for Meso-Rex bypass (MRB) in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO). MATERIALS AND METHODS: From October 2014 to July 2024, children with EHPVO after MRB were retrospectively analyzed. The number of MRB, the type of bypass vessel, and the position of the lower anastomosis were collected. Predictive variables include the diameter of the connection between the left and right portal veins, the Rex vein (RV) diameter, the number of RV branches, the diameter of the thickest RV branch, and the bypass-to-superior mesenteric vein (SMV) angle, which were measured by Contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) one week after MRB. The upper and lower anastomotic stenosis were diagnosed by Ultrasound and CECT one year after MRB. RESULTS: A total of 153 children (median age 72 months, 87 males) were included in this study. Univariate factors include the number of MRBs, the type of bypass vessel, and CECT variables (except the diameter of the thickest RV branch). Numbers of MRB and RV branches were retained in the final model for upper anastomotic stenosis. The combination of MRB > 1 and RV branches ≤ 4 predicts it post-MRB with 75% sensitivity, 86.4% specificity, and an area under the receiver operator characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.832. The bypass-to-SMV angle ≤ 110° predicts lower anastomotic stenosis after MRB with 90% sensitivity, 73.39% specificity, and AUC 0.847. CONCLUSIONS: Associated factors are useful for early postoperative risk stratification. Moreover, the type of bypass vessel and the bypass-to-SMV angle could be used to inform future surgical technique refinement. FindingsAssociated factors include bypass-to-SMV angle, number of MRB, RV branches and diameter, left-right portal vein connection diameter, and type of bypass vessel. Clinical RelevanceAssociated factors are useful for early postoperative risk stratification. Moreover, the internal jugular vein as the bridge vessel and the bypass-to-SMV angle > 110° could be used to optimize the surgical plan for a better outcome.

title: Pelvic vein embolization using different embolic agents for the treatment of pelvic venous insufficiency: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Embolization of insufficient pelvic veins has been established as the standard first-line therapy in women with chronic pain due to pelvic venous disorder; however, the clinically available embolic devices vary widely, with coils, vascular plugs, glue, and sclerosants or combinations of these devices being the most common. This study aims to evaluate the ability of different devices to reduce pain and their individual rates of success and complications. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted using PubMed, ScienceDirect, Cochrane, and ClinicalTrials.gov for studies published on the embolization of insufficient pelvic veins up until November 2025. The primary outcome measure was the effect of embolization on pelvic pain as measured using visual analog scale (VAS). The secondary end points were the technical and clinical success rates as well as the recurrence, complication, and reintervention rates. RESULTS: A total of 28 studies met the inclusion criteria, totaling 2688 patients across 34 individual cohorts who were grouped into five treatment categories. The technical success rate was high across all the embolization methods, ranging from 98.6% to 100%, and the clinical success rate ranged from 68.3% to 100%. All the endovascular treatment options led to a reduction in pain as measured using VAS, which ranged from 4.67 (95% confidence interval [CI], 3.87-5.47) points reduction in the sclerosant-only group to 6.12 (95% CI, 5.46-6.78) in the vascular plugs group. The clinical success rate was the highest in the sclerosant-only and plugs groups at 97.5% (95% CI, 93.7-99.3) and 94.7% (95% CI, 86.9-98.5), respectively. Complications, especially in the form of device migration, most frequently appeared in the coils group at 2.63% (95% CI, 1.76-3.78) and least frequently in the sclerosant-only group at 0.45% (95% CI, 0.01-2.48). Sclerosants led to the lowest recurrence at 1.69% (95% CI, 0.49-4.87) but the highest number of reinterventions at 13.3% (95% CI, 5.1-26.8). Vascular plugs resulted in few complications (0.6% [95% CI, 0.07-2.15]), as well as low recurrence (3.47% [95% CI, 1.6-6.49]) and reintervention (2.59% [95% CI, 1.12-5.04]). CONCLUSIONS: All the embolization methods showed excellent technical success rates and marked reduction in pain as measured using VAS. Using coils seems to be associated with the highest occurrence of device migration. The vascular plugs and sclerosant-only groups had high clinical success with low complication rates. Due to the small sample sizes and lack of inter-group comparisons, the conclusions should be viewed cautiously.

title: Optimizing the management of venous disease: Expert consensus from a multinational panel of phlebology specialists.
abstract: Chronic venous disease and varicose veins (VV) are highly prevalent yet remain inconsistently managed despite existing guidelines, with variability in treatment selection, patient stratification, and use of conservative therapies. This multinational initiative sought to establish expert consensus on key clinical questions in venous disease management. A Delphi-like process involved 38 phlebologists from 15 countries across Europe, North Africa, and Central Asia. Four thematic workshops addressed interventional and conservative approaches for both chronic venous disease and VV. Twenty predefined questions were discussed, and resulting statements were rated on a 5-point Likert scale, with consensus defined as ≥75% agreement. Of 34 proposed statements, 30 (88%) achieved consensus. The panel emphasized that treatment decisions should be driven primarily by symptoms and quality of life rather than anatomy alone. Endovenous procedures were supported for symptomatic disease, with endovenous laser ablation and radiofrequency ablation considered equivalent for VV. Diosmin-based venoactive drugs, often combined with compression, were endorsed across Clinical, Etiologic, Anatomic, and Pathophysiologic classes for symptom relief, although adherence to conservative therapy remains limited. This consensus provides practical guidance for individualized care and highlights unmet needs in risk stratification, adherence, and long-term comparative outcomes.

abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute severe ulcerative colitis (ASUC) is a life-threatening complication of ulcerative colitis that requires hospitalization and prompt guideline-directed management.
